report.warm_baseline: the exact first-complete-cycle scalar fixture record

caller_contract: The fixture is one fresh Linux/AArch64 process and calls init once with its original thread's nonzero AT_PAGESZ value.
Every allocation, reallocation, and free is serialized on that original thread.

After the original thread frees every adapter allocation, one fresh pthread may make one pointer-free narrow worker round trip or one pointer-private persistent mixed-local worker round trip; either creates and finishes one later-main page engine before its normal worker teardown.

The persistent worker keeps one engine through multiple simultaneously live small, medium, large, singleton, and multi-page singleton allocations, checks their contents, locally reuses freed small and medium blocks, and frees every block before engine finish; no pointer crosses the worker boundary.

After the original thread frees every adapter allocation, one fresh pthread may become remote-free owner A. The adapter starts and joins two private publisher pthreads B/C; only opaque logical publication capabilities reach them, A false-collects and reuses both remote blocks while still live, and then A frees every block before normal teardown.

After the original thread frees every adapter allocation, one fresh pthread may become mixed regular-page owner A. The adapter keeps three direct-small clients from one source page, a non-direct-small page, two distinct full medium pages, a one-client force-empty large page, a distinct two-client live large page, one live arena singleton, and one live OS-aligned singleton in one aggregate route, then suspends A's exact page engine into private compiler TLS and invokes ordinary post-destructor runtime finish. That dispatch resumes only A's matching engine and runs source collection: it makes the first medium page mapped, releases the now-empty force-empty large page, and leaves the unchanged second medium page source-unmapped; the arena member stays private through its PageMap-only raw terminal tail and the OS member through its static-main list and clipped-mapping tail. A distinct fresh B receives only the opaque post-exit route. B directly frees one existing direct-small client after claiming that source page's low owner bit; joined C and D each receive one scoped producer for the remaining distinct same-page clients, publish in separate joined turns, and return before B's existing collector consumes the two-node remote chain. B terminally releases every surviving member, completes B's own no-page runtime attachment, and only then returns A's worker-admission proof; A cannot take the no-page finalizer while that route remains live.

After the original thread frees every adapter allocation, one fresh pthread may become the source owner A of one initially-nonfull mapped-regular page with two private live clients and one returned local free. The existing reclamation export alternates source-valid sole-medium and direct-small predecessors without adding a C operation: the medium source's exit collector makes the returned block the route's immediate head, while the direct-small source validates and clears its complete rounded direct-cache image plus immediate head. A suspends that engine into the same private compiler-TLS owner and ordinary post-destructor finish dispatch; after A's Theap/TLD teardown, joined B receives only an opaque route, attaches through the runtime, reclaims and uses A's exact page, drains it empty, and completes B's own page lifecycle before returning A's terminal admission proof.

After every scheduled worker joins, the original thread may request one test-only scalar lifecycle audit. It reports process/page-owner readiness and aggregate PageMap, arena registry, live-TLD, metadata-capability, shared-Theap, regular-abandoned, and OS-abandoned-list state only; it cannot identify or operate on a pointer, page, route, allocator, or release capability. The first complete schedule cycle warms immutable capacity; every later cycle and the final ticket-zero allocation/free must reproduce that quiescent snapshot.
Only current pointers returned by this adapter may reach its realloc or free entry points.
No shutdown is exposed: the permanent source-shaped ticket-zero page owner remains live until process exit.
The adapter exports no malloc, free, or mi_* ELF symbol and never selects crabc-libc's production backend.
fixture_observations: init, malloc, realloc, zalloc, and free preserve the caller's errno on their successful paths
the first ordinary allocation activates one real ticket-zero page-owner allocation
after all exact allocations free, the owner releases only its Rust PageMap lifecycle lease
one fresh worker can borrow that dormant published pair for the retained narrow scoped page-engine round trip and finish its normal attachment

the default three, or one caller-selected bounded count of, fresh workers can each retain one engine through the pointer-private mixed local small/medium/large/singleton/multi-page workload, locally reuse freed small and medium blocks, free all blocks, and restore normal attachment teardown

the default three, or one caller-selected bounded count of, fresh remote-free owners A can each create and join B/C, publish two exact full-small-page blocks through the real remote head, false-collect and reuse both while A stays live, free all blocks, and restore normal attachment teardown

the default three, or one caller-selected bounded count of, fresh mixed owner-exit workers A each keep three direct-small clients from one source page, a non-direct-small page, two distinct `BIN_FULL` medium pages, a one-client force-empty large page, a distinct two-client live large page, one live arena singleton, and one live OS-aligned singleton in the same aggregate traversal, then suspend that live engine into private TLS and enter ordinary post-destructor finish; joined pre-exit remote frees make the first medium nonfull and the force-empty large page empty during source collection, retain the unchanged second medium source-unmapped, detach a genuinely mixed regular Theap, and let a distinct joined fresh B claim the direct-small source low owner bit for its first post-exit free while scoped joined C and D each atomically append one remaining same-page private client in separate joined turns; B's ordinary collector consumes the resulting two-node remote chain before B releases every remaining regular, arena, and OS client—including the arena PageMap-only tail and private-list removal before clipped OS mapping release—and finishes B's own no-page attachment before A's admission becomes fork-quiescent

the default three, or one caller-selected bounded count of, fresh mapped-regular reclamation workers A alternate an initially-nonfull sole-medium page with one returned local free and a source-valid direct-small page with the same private-client shape; both suspend into the same private TLS/ordinary-finish dispatch. The medium source transfers its free into the immediate head, while the direct-small source validates and clears its complete rounded direct-cache image plus immediate head; a joined opaque B then attaches, reclaims/uses that exact page, drains all private clients, and finishes B's PageMap/TLD lifecycle before the typed proof makes A fork-quiescent

the fixture accepts no arguments for its default three worker cycles and default unsigned-64-bit schedule seed, or at most one each of `--worker-cycles N` for decimal N in 1..1024 and `--stress-seed SEED` for a base-0 unsigned-64-bit literal in either order; every cycle executes each of the four pointer-private worker routes exactly once in a deterministic seed-shuffled order. The first completed cycle is the scalar lifecycle-audit warmup; each later cycle and the final ticket-zero allocation/free must match that audit's quiescent baseline. `allocator --churn` selects 128 with seed `0xd1b54a32d192ed03` under a 30-second watchdog, while opt-in `allocator --soak` selects 1024 with seed `0x94d049bb133111eb` under a 180-second watchdog
ticket zero reactivates afterward through the same first arena

compile_requirements.compiler: musl-gcc from the pinned Linux/AArch64 container
